topic: Coffee consumption improves long-term memory formation in elderly adults over age 65

referenced_sources.title: Acute Caffeine Effects on Reaction Time During Simulated Driving in Young Adults
referenced_sources.abstract: This study examined the short-term effects of a single 200mg caffeine dose on reaction time and alertness in 40 healthy university students (mean age 21) during a 30-minute simulated driving task. Caffeine significantly improved reaction time compared to placebo within the first hour post-consumption. No measures of memory, cognition beyond alertness, or long-term outcomes were assessed.

referenced_sources.title: Historical Review of Coffee Trade Economics in the 19th Century
referenced_sources.abstract: This paper traces the economic history of coffee as a global commodity during the 19th century, focusing on colonial trade routes, pricing structures, and labor systems. No biological, medical, or cognitive claims are made.
